comparison: Both address the excess of ancient polymorphisms (C37-C44). OpenEval finds the evidence comprehensive and strongly supportive, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about robustness to demographic model variation, requesting additional validation of parameter sensitivity.

OpenEval R1 includes claims about ruling out ancestral structure and introgression (C45-C49), which peer R2 evaluates separately as supported. Peer reviewers accept the logic used to exclude these alternative explanations.

Both evaluate the categorization methodology (C50-C57). OpenEval finds the systematic pipeline well-validated with convergent dating methods, while peer reviewers express substantial uncertainty about classification reliability, questioning the LD threshold and differentiation between ancient and recurrent cases.

Both address balancing selection detection (C58-C63). OpenEval finds the statistical evidence appropriate and the novel candidates appropriately conservative, while peer reviewers question whether these represent truly novel balancing selection loci versus linkage to known SNV loci.

Both evaluate functional enrichment claims (C64-C65). OpenEval finds the statistical evidence clear and methodology sound, while peer reviewers indicate the current evidence may not be sufficiently strong, requesting additional statistical support to strengthen the '27%' claim.

Both address phenotypic enrichment (C66-C67). OpenEval finds the enrichment values and statistical significance appropriate, while peer reviewers group this with functional enrichment concerns, suggesting the evidence needs strengthening.

Both evaluate the overdominance analysis (C94-C97, C105-C106). OpenEval finds the empirical evidence and simulation work well-supported, while peer reviewers accept the general conclusion but request verification through allele frequency distributions to confirm the pattern is inconsistent with overdominance.

Both address deletions versus SNVs comparison (C83-C87). OpenEval finds the comparative data and inference about deleteriousness well-supported, while peer reviewers do not challenge this analysis, treating it as supported evidence.

Both evaluate deletion size distribution findings (C88-C93). OpenEval finds the statistical evidence and paradoxical pattern well-documented, while peer reviewers accept this analysis without challenge, requesting only methodological clarification about length distributions.

Both address specific gene family examples (C68-C73). OpenEval finds the examples well-supported though the fine-tuning hypothesis remains speculative, while peer reviewers do not challenge these descriptive findings, treating them as supporting evidence.

Both evaluate isoform switching mechanisms (C74-C82, C107). OpenEval finds the examples documented but functional interpretations speculative, while peer reviewers accept these as descriptive findings illustrating functional consequences without challenge.

OpenEval R11 addresses specific claims about dosage compensation (C98-C100), finding them appropriately supported though somewhat speculative. Peer R10 groups broader conclusions including C100, indicating these depend on resolution of specific methodological concerns.
Both address background and contextual claims (C1, C10-C36). Both evaluations find these well-cited and appropriate as foundational context, not novel findings requiring evaluation.

Both address concluding synthesis claims (C9, C108-C109). OpenEval finds these appropriately cautious and supported by convergent evidence, while peer reviewers indicate these broad conclusions depend on resolution of essential revisions regarding model robustness, novelty assessment, and statistical enrichment.

OpenEval R4 addresses functional enrichment (C6, C64-C65, C103-C104), while peer R10 groups these with broader conclusions requiring essential revisions. Partial overlap in claims but different scopes of evaluation.

OpenEval R5 addresses phenotypic enrichment (C7, C66-C67), while peer R10 includes C7 in broader conclusions requiring essential revisions. Minimal overlap but related to overall functional significance claims.

OpenEval R3 addresses balancing selection detection (C3, C58-C63, C102), while peer R10 includes C102 in broader conclusions. Peer reviewers indicate overall conclusions depend on resolving concerns about novelty versus linkage.

OpenEval R1 addresses ancient polymorphism excess (C2, C37-C49, C101), while peer R10 includes C101 in broader conclusions. Peer reviewers indicate overall conclusions depend on resolving model robustness concerns.
